trap-bar-deadlift.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
trap-bar-deadlift.focus: Builds the hip and leg drive that gets you out of the crouch and into a throw-down. Keep the chest proud so your back stays quiet after a long game of squatting.
cues: Feet hip-width, mid-foot under the handles. Hips down, chest up, lats tight, big brace.
Push the floor away. Bar speed stays steady, hips and shoulders rise together.
Squeeze glutes to a tall lockout. No leaning back. Lower with control.

tempo-goblet-squat.name: Tempo Goblet / Front Squat
tempo-goblet-squat.focus: A slow lowering phase and a 3-second pause in the hole builds the strength and control for your receiving stance without loading the knees.
cues: Weight at the chest, elbows up, feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out. Brace.
Sit between your hips. Knees track over toes, heels heavy. Pause, chest tall.
Drive up fast through the whole foot. Stand tall and reset.

copenhagen-plank.name: Copenhagen Plank
copenhagen-plank.focus: Adductor strength protects the groin from the wide, low stance and the lateral blocking a catcher does all game.
cues: Top foot on the bench, elbow under the shoulder, bottom leg tucked under.
Lift hips until the body is a straight line. Squeeze the inner thigh and hold.
Lower under control. Switch sides. Stop the set when the hips sag.

bulgarian-split-squat.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
bulgarian-split-squat.focus: Single-leg strength and hip mobility for the squat-and-throw pattern. Fixes the left-right gaps that creep into a catcher's crouch.
cues: Rear foot on the bench, front foot far enough out that the shin stays vertical.
Drop straight down. Torso slightly forward, front knee tracks over the toes.
Drive through the front heel to stand. Keep hips square.

seated-calf-raises.name: Seated Calf Raise
seated-calf-raises.focus: Strong calves and soleus keep the ankles healthy and let you sit in the crouch longer without the lower leg tightening.
cues: Pad on the lower thigh, balls of the feet on the platform, heels hanging.
Sink the heels slowly to a full stretch at the bottom.
Press up high onto the big toe and squeeze for a beat.

landmine-press.name: Landmine Press
landmine-press.focus: A shoulder-friendly press that follows the natural arc of the arm. Builds pressing strength without jamming the throwing shoulder overhead.
cues: Bar end at the shoulder, split stance, ribs down, glutes tight.
Lower the bar slowly back to the shoulder. Keep the elbow in front of the ribs.
Press up and slightly forward to a long arm. Shoulder blade glides around the ribcage.

chest-supported-row.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
chest-supported-row.focus: Pulling strength for the rear shoulder and upper back, the muscles that decelerate the arm after every throw.
cues: Chest on the pad, arms long, neutral neck. Shoulder blades relaxed.
Row elbows toward the back pockets and pinch the shoulder blades together.
Lower slowly to a full stretch. No shrugging.

half-kneeling-pulldown.name: Half-Kneeling Cable Pull-Down
half-kneeling-pulldown.focus: Lat strength from a stable half-kneel. Builds the pull for the throwing arm while the position trains hip stability.
cues: Down knee on the pad, glute squeezed, tall spine, arm reaching up to the handle.
Pull the elbow down to the ribs. Ribs stay down, no leaning back.
Control the handle up to a full reach. Keep the glute tight.

face-pulls.name: Face Pulls w/ External Rotation
face-pulls.focus: Rotator cuff and rear delt work that keeps the throwing shoulder healthy through a long season of throws to second.
cues: Rope at forehead height, thumbs back, elbows high, slight lean back.
Pull the rope to the eyebrows, then rotate the hands up like a double biceps pose.
Reverse the rotation and return slowly. Do not shrug.

pallof-press.name: Pallof Press
pallof-press.focus: Anti-rotation core strength so you can stay square and stable when you throw from awkward positions behind the plate.
cues: Stand side-on to the cable, feet shoulder-width, hands at the chest, ribs stacked over hips.
Press the handle straight out and hold. Resist the cable pulling you around.
Bring hands back to the chest slowly without twisting.

catcher-box-jumps.name: Box Jumps from Catcher Crouch
catcher-box-jumps.focus: Explosive hip extension from your actual game position. Trains the first step out of the crouch for blocking, bunt coverage and throw-downs.
cues: Settle into your real catcher crouch facing the box. Weight on the balls of your feet.
Load by dropping the hips an inch and swinging the arms back.
Jump up and land softly in a quarter squat on the whole box. Step down, reset.

lateral-skater-bounds.name: Lateral Skater Bounds
lateral-skater-bounds.focus: Lateral power and landing control for blocking balls in the dirt and sliding to cover wide pitches.
cues: Stand on one leg, slight hip hinge, arms ready to swing.
Push off sideways with the outside leg, swing the arms across for balance.
Land on the opposite leg and stick it for two seconds. Knee over the toes.

romanian-deadlift.name: Romanian Deadlift
romanian-deadlift.focus: Hamstring and glute strength for a powerful throw-down and healthy hamstrings from all that time in the squat.
cues: Stand tall with the bar at the thighs, soft knees, shoulders back.
Push the hips straight back. Bar slides down the legs. Stop at a hamstring stretch.
Drive the hips forward and squeeze the glutes. Do not lean back at the top.

heavy-sled-pushes.name: Heavy Sled Pushes
heavy-sled-pushes.focus: Builds leg drive and conditioning with no eccentric load, so you recover fast for the next session.
cues: Hands on the high handles, arms locked, body at a 45 degree lean, hips low.
Short powerful steps. Push the ground behind you and keep the back flat.
Finish the 20 yards, stand up tall, walk back to recover.

dead-bugs.name: Weighted / Banded Dead Bugs
dead-bugs.focus: Deep core control that keeps the low back flat and protected while the arms and legs move, which matters in a long, repeated crouch.
cues: On your back, hips and knees at 90 degrees, arms up, low back pressed into the floor.
Slowly extend the opposite arm and leg. Back stays flat the whole time.
Return to the start with control and switch sides.

med-ball-scoop-toss.name: Med Ball Rotational Scoop Toss
med-ball-scoop-toss.focus: Trains the hip-to-shoulder rotation used in your throw and your swing. Power should come from the legs and hips, not the arms.
cues: Athletic stance side-on to the wall, ball at the back hip, knees soft.
Load into the back hip and sit slightly. Eyes on the target.
Rotate hard through the hips and let the ball fly off the front hip into the wall.

push-up-plus.name: Push-Up Plus
push-up-plus.focus: The extra push at the top activates the serratus, which stabilizes the shoulder blade for throwing and for blocking.
cues: Hands under the shoulders, body in a straight plank, glutes tight.
Lower the chest to the floor under control. Elbows at about 45 degrees.
Press up, then keep pushing the floor away so the shoulder blades spread wide.

neutral-grip-pullups.name: Chin-Ups / Neutral-Grip Pull-Ups
neutral-grip-pullups.focus: Upper-back and lat strength, along with the shoulder health that comes from hanging and pulling, for the arm that throws every pitch.
cues: Dead hang with shoulder blades down and back. Legs together.
Pull the elbows down until your chin clears the bar. Chest to the bar.
Lower slowly to a full hang. Stop the set one rep before form breaks.

bottoms-up-kb-carry.name: Bottoms-Up Kettlebell Carry
bottoms-up-kb-carry.focus: Grip and rotator cuff stability under constant tension. Teaches the shoulder to stay centered, which is what it has to do on every throw.
cues: Clean the bell up so it is balanced upside down, wrist stacked, elbow tucked in.
Walk tall and slow. Keep the bell steady and the shoulder packed down.
Finish the 30 yards, lower the bell with control, switch arms.

band-ytw-raises.name: Band Y-T-W Raises
band-ytw-raises.focus: Light, high-quality work for the lower traps and rear delts. Keeps the shoulder blades moving well after repeated throws.
cues: Light band in both hands, ribs down, tall posture, arms at your sides.
Raise the arms into a Y, then T, then W. Thumbs up, shoulder blades down and back.
Lower slowly. Keep the neck relaxed and do not shrug.

trap-bar-jump-shrugs.name: Light Trap Bar Jump Shrugs
trap-bar-jump-shrugs.focus: Fast triple extension without heavy loading, which keeps your power high while your legs recover for games.
cues: Light load on the trap bar, stand tall, soft knees, shoulders back.
Dip into a quarter squat and keep the chest up.
Jump as high as possible and shrug at the top. Land softly and reset.

goblet-squat-pause.name: Goblet Squat (2s Pause)
goblet-squat-pause.focus: Keeps your squat pattern sharp in-season with minimal fatigue. The pause builds control in the bottom position.
cues: Dumbbell at the chest, elbows in, feet shoulder-width, brace.
Sit down between the hips and pause. Chest tall, knees out.
Stand up fast through the heels.

half-kneeling-landmine-press.name: Half-Kneeling Landmine Press
half-kneeling-landmine-press.focus: Shoulder-friendly pressing strength from a stable base. Half-kneeling keeps the hips and core working while the arm presses.
cues: Down knee under the hip, glute squeezed, bar at the shoulder, ribs down.
Lower the bar slowly back to the shoulder. Stay tall.
Press up and forward to a long arm without leaning back.

inverted-rows.name: TRX / Inverted Row
inverted-rows.focus: Pulls the shoulder blades back and balances all the forward-reaching you do as a catcher. Easy on the joints in-season.
cues: Hang under the handles, body straight from heels to head, arms long.
Pull the chest to the handles and squeeze the shoulder blades together.
Lower slowly to full arm extension. Keep hips up.

side-plank-abduction.name: Side Plank w/ Hip Abduction
side-plank-abduction.focus: Lateral hip and core strength for stable knees and hips in the crouch and for sliding to block.
cues: Elbow under the shoulder, feet stacked, hips lifted into a straight line.
Raise the top leg toward the ceiling while keeping the hips up.
Lower the leg slowly. Keep the hips high for the whole set.

med-ball-slams.name: Med Ball Side-to-Side Slams
med-ball-slams.focus: Light rotational power for midweek that primes the hips and trunk without taxing the legs.
cues: Athletic stance, ball overhead on one side, hips loaded to that side.
Rotate the hips and slam the ball down hard on the opposite side.
Catch the bounce or pick it up, reset, and slam to the other side.

single-leg-rdl.name: Single-Leg RDL
single-leg-rdl.focus: Balance and hamstring strength on one leg. A common area of strain for catchers, so it keeps the hips honest.
cues: Stand on one leg with a soft knee, weight in the mid-foot, weight in the opposite hand.
Hinge at the hip, the free leg travels back, and the back stays flat. Hips stay square.
Squeeze the glute to stand tall. Do not rotate the hips.

band-pull-apart-er.name: Band Pull-Aparts & External Rotations
band-pull-apart-er.focus: Rotator cuff and upper-back activation. A quick, low-fatigue way to keep the throwing shoulder healthy midweek.
cues: Light band at chest height, arms straight, shoulder blades relaxed.
Pull the band apart to the chest, then rotate the forearms outward with elbows at the sides.
Return slowly. Keep the ribs down and the neck relaxed.

hip-switch-couch-stretch.name: 90/90 Hip Switches & Couch Stretch
hip-switch-couch-stretch.focus: Opens the hips and quads after the week of crouching so your stance is deep and comfortable.
cues: Sit in 90/90, torso tall. Then set a back knee against the wall for the couch stretch.
Squeeze the glute of the back leg and breathe slowly through the front of the hip.
Switch sides smoothly and repeat.

hip-90-90.name: 90/90 Hip Transitions
hip-90-90.focus: Rotation in both hips for a deep, comfortable crouch and for smoother transitions into the throwing position.
cues: Sit with both knees at 90 degrees, shins to either side, chest tall.
Lift the knees and rotate to the other side with control. Hands stay light.
Reset tall and repeat. Ten smooth switches.

ankle-rocks.name: Half-Kneeling Ankle Dorsiflexion Rocks
ankle-rocks.focus: Ankle mobility is what keeps your heels down in the crouch. It is also the first thing that tightens during a long stretch of catching.
cues: Half-kneeling with the front foot a few inches from the wall, heel flat.
Drive the front knee over the toes toward the wall. Heel stays down.
Rock back and repeat ten times each side.

adductor-rock-backs.name: Adductor Rock-Backs
adductor-rock-backs.focus: Opens the inner thighs so the wide receiving stance does not feel pinched and the groin stays healthy.
cues: On all fours, one leg out to the side with the foot flat, spine neutral.
Sit the hips back toward the heel, keeping the back straight. Feel the inner thigh stretch.
Return forward and repeat ten times each side.

open-book-rotations.name: Open-Book Thoracic Rotations
open-book-rotations.focus: Upper-back rotation that lets the shoulders turn freely when you throw, without borrowing motion from the low back.
cues: Lie on your side, hips and knees at 90 degrees, arms straight in front.
Open the top arm up and back, following it with your eyes. Knees stay stacked.
Return and repeat eight times each side.

shoulder-stretch.name: Sleeper / Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
shoulder-stretch.focus: Post-game only. Restores the back of the throwing shoulder after a heavy throwing day. Gentle, never painful.
cues: Lie on the throwing side with the elbow at 90 degrees in front of the shoulder.
Use the other hand to gently press the forearm toward the floor. Stop at a mild stretch.
Release slowly. Hold 30 seconds, then switch.
